# Challenge Patterns

## Predict Before You Run
Show code/configuration or a model change. Require a prediction before execution. Run it, compare the observed result, then explain the mechanism.

## Break It / Fix It
Start from a working system, introduce one deliberate defect, observe the symptom, diagnose the cause, repair it, and explain why the repair worked.

## Model Detective
Provide learning curves, metrics, logs, outputs, or misclassified examples while hiding the implementation. Ask participants to infer the likely problem and evidence.

## Make It Fail on Purpose
Ask participants to deliberately produce overfitting, instability, leakage, or another failure. This makes the failure pattern memorable before teaching the remedy.

## Before / After
Capture a baseline, make one targeted change, show the new result, and require an explanation of the difference.

## You Get One Experiment
Provide limited compute/time and several possible interventions. Require one choice supported by evidence, then run it.

## Engineering Trade-off
Present two models with different accuracy/latency/size/cost properties. Require a choice for a stated scenario and a defense of the decision.

## Transfer-Learning Race
Compare training from scratch with adapting a pretrained model. Score outcome, time, compute, and quality of explanation rather than accuracy alone.
